payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent teardown audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee and retracted the earlier 12,000-cycle claim. The battery’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry has a hard operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.

FLAGS: Source A and the unpublished pre-audit draft state “12,000 cycles,” while finalized Source C governs with “8,400 cycles” and explicitly retracts the earlier figure.
VERDICT: APPROVE
